articles.title: Conjura española para reconquistar la BCL: “Todos quieren ganarla, hay muchísimo nivel”
articles.standfirst: Arranca la 11ª temporada con cuatro equipos españoles: Joventut, Surne Bilbao Basket, UCAM Murcia y Unicaja
articles.summary: Arranca la 11ª temporada con cuatro equipos españoles: Joventut, Surne Bilbao Basket, UCAM Murcia y Unicaja
articles.body: Joventut, Surne Bilbao Basket, UCAM Murcia y Unicaja arrancan una nueva aventura en una Basketball Champions League que cumple once temporadas consolidada como una referencia continental y manteniendo una de sus señas de identidad: premiar el rendimiento y la meritocracia deportiva. Tras el triunfo del Rytas Vilnius en la inolvidable Final Four de Badalona, los cuatro españoles apuntan a lo más alto para devolver a España un trofeo que ha ganado en seis de sus diez primeras ediciones: “Todo el mundo quiere ganar la BCL”. El cartel de participantes es un auténtico lujo afrontando un mínimo de 194 partidos en 8 meses de máxima emoción con 32 equipos arrancando la Fase Regular. El campeón de cada uno de los 8 grupos se clasificará directamente al Round of 16 mientras que el segundo y el tercero jugarán unos play in al mejor de tres encuentros para obtener una plaza. En esta nueva fase con cuatro grupos de cuatro equipos, los dos mejores se clasifican para unos cuartos de final previos a una Final Four que promete fuetes emociones de nuevo. Kaiser Gates afronta la nueva temporada con un objetivo claro: competir por todo. “Queremos ganar todo lo que podamos. Queremos ganar la competición entera si es posible. Ese es siempre nuestro objetivo”, asegura el jugador de UCAM Murcia. “Hay muchos equipos con muchísimo talento y cada año se eleva el listón de la competición”, dice. Gates también destaca el crecimiento de la Basketball Champions League y el nivel de sus participantes. “Creo que la BCL hace un gran trabajo promocionando su competición y en cuanto a marketing y redes la exposición es tremenda poniendo en valor el trabajo de los jugadores y de los equipos. Hay grandísimos equipos que participan y creo que es una gran competición en la que estar”. Además no oculta un deseo: “Sería genial poder albergar la Final Four en Murcia”. Bilbao Basket da esta temporada un paso más en Europa después de su éxito en la FIBA Europe Cup. Para Luke Petrasek, aquella experiencia puede ser una buena base para afrontar ahora una competición de mayor exigencia. “El año pasado nuestro equipo tenía un objetivo y era ganar el campeonato. Eso nos llevó a mantenernos disciplinados durante toda la temporada”, explica. “Estoy muy contento de que pudiéramos conseguirlo. Ahora damos el salto a la BCL y creo que volver a tener éxito sería increíble para nuestro equipo. Tenemos muchos jugadores de alto nivel y queremos seguir ganando partidos”. Petrasek, que ya conoce la competición de una etapa anterior, tiene muy clara la dimensión que ha alcanzado el torneo. “La Basketball Champions League tiene una reputación increíble en toda Europa. Todo el mundo sabe que los equipos que están aquí compiten al máximo nivel”. “Todo lo que rodea a la competición, también el marketing, es de primer nivel. El torneo está muy bien hecho y por eso los equipos quieren estar aquí. Tener éxito en la BCL da mucho reconocimiento al club y a los jugadores. La BCL cuenta con una altísima reputación en Europa, todo lo que rodea a la BCL desde lo deportivo al marketing es de un altísimo nivel y la organización está muy bien lograda. Por eso todos los equipos quieren estar”. El estadounidense reconoce además que el salto respecto a la FIBA Europecup será importante. “La competición será mejor, eso no es ningún secreto. Pero jugando en la ACB te enfrentas a muchos equipos de Champions League y eso te da una idea del nivel y de la intensidad”. La Penya inicia una nueva aventura europea con ambición máxima y Eli Ndiaye lo deja claro: “La Basketball Champions League es una competición que todo el mundo quiere ganar”. El jugador verdinegro afronta esta nueva etapa con ambición máxima en todas las competiciones: “Para mí todo es un reto. He venido a la Penya para intentar ganarlo todo y competir al máximo. La Supercopa, la BCL, la ACB… todo lo que podamos ganar. Estoy preparado para todos los retos”. El Joventut llega además a una competición que conoce bien desde fuera, después de haber acogido en Badalona la última Final Four. Esta temporada quiere pasar de anfitrión a protagonista con Ricky Rubio al frente: “Estoy muy motivado y esperanzado con lo que podemos lograr. Hay cosas que yo no puedo controlar pero sí disfrutar del baloncesto. Y aquí con Ricky, todos sabemos lo grande que es, un jugador enorme que puede cambiar partidos”. Unicaja regresa a una competición que ha marcado buena parte de sus últimos años. Campeón en 2024 y 2025 y tercero la pasada temporada, el conjunto malagueño vuelve a partir entre los equipos con aspiraciones con un renovado proyecto y un Willy Hernangómez motivadísimo con ganas de descubrir una nueva experiencia: “Todo el mundo me habla maravillas de la Basketball Champions League”. “El nivel es muy alto, no hay más que comprobar el listado de equipos participantes con mucho nombre en toda Europa. Unicaja ha ganado dos seguidos, que no es nada fácil, y el año pasado se quedó a las puertas de la tercera BCL seguida”, cuenta el pívot. El internacional español aterriza en Málaga con la ambición de prolongar el éxito reciente del club en la competición: “Queremos empezar bien, seguir creciendo y mejorando y, ojalá, volver a ganarla para nuestra afición”. “Yo estoy feliz, disfrutando, muy motivado y con ganas de ayudar al equipo y a todos mis compañeros en todo lo que pueda”, explica.

articles.title: Thomas Müller excludes Harry Kane from Ballon d’Or favorites list
articles.summary: Former Bayern Munich star Thomas Müller has named Michael Olise and Kylian Mbappé as his two leading candidates for the 2026 Ballon d’Or, notably leaving for...
articles.body:
Former Bayern Munich star Thomas Müller has named Michael Olise and Kylian Mbappé as his two leading candidates for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, notably leaving former teammate Harry Kane out of his selections.

Writing in his newsletter, the Vancouver Whitecaps forward explained that Olise and Mbappé were the two players whose individual performances had impressed him most."For me, there are two candidates whose individual performances have impressed me the most, and they are Michael Olise and his brilliant partner at the World Cup, Kylian Mbappé," Müller said. "The two combine spectacular play with a real goal threat. In the finer details, they manage to be efficient with their finesse and power while making the whole thing look incredibly effortless. To me, that's the kind of material you need to be the world's best footballer. You simply need that touch of magic."Müller did not explicitly explain why Kane failed to make his top two. The England captain nevertheless remains among the leading contenders after another prolific campaign with Bayern.

Müller continues to rave about Michael Olise

Olise, meanwhile, continues to impress his former Bayern teammate. Müller highlighted the French winger's recent performance in the 7-0 Bundesliga victory over Union Berlin, in which Olise once again demonstrated his threat from distance."It's nothing new, how he converts those strikes from outside the box, and yet it's always a spectacle," Müller said.Olise and Mbappé are both among the nominees for this year's award alongside Kane and several other leading contenders. Barcelona star Lamine Yamal is also expected to feature prominently after finishing behind Ousmane Dembélé in last year's voting.The 2026 Ballon d'Or winner will be announced in London on October 26.Müller himself remains in strong form following his move to Vancouver. The 2014 World Cup winner recently extended his contract with the Whitecaps and joked in his newsletter that things have been going well in front of goal."For me personally, things are going pretty well in front of the opposition goal," Müller said. "At times, I've even been accused of showing dynamism."

articles.title: Diego Forlan returns to Kolkata, India looking to instil his managerial philosophy
articles.summary: TimesofIndia.com in Kolkata: Diego Forlan with his locks of golden hair is unmissable.
articles.body: TimesofIndia.com in Kolkata: Diego Forlan with his locks of golden hair is unmissable. The FIFA World Football Museum sports one strange piece of memorabilia: a hairband worn by the Uruguayan during the 2010 World Cup where he finished joint top-scorer after scoring five goals. On Monday a similar hairband was sported by the interim Uruguay national team manager in Kolakat, hundreds of kilometres from those exploits in South Africa.He's been here before. Him and his distinct white hairband. Except in a different capacity. The 47-year-old spent one season with Mumbai City FC in the Indian Super League (ISL) in 2016 and played twice in Kolkata, at the Rabindra Sarobar Stadium. On Tuesday evening, it will be the Salt Lake Stadium which will be lit for the interim Uruguay manager and his team as they face India in a FIFA friendly.Named as the interim manager after Marcelo Bielsa stepped down, these are big shoes to fill. Additionally, he's coming in in difficult times.The two-time World Cup champions were knocked out early in the extravaganza in North America after failing to pick up a win in a group that featured Cape Verde and Saudi Arabia. Before the final game against Spain, the squad clashed with Bielsa over tactical approach. With the World Cup ending on a disastrous note, the Uruguayan Football Association (AUF) cancelled the team's chartered private return flights, forcing players to return home on commercial flights as a disciplinary reprimand."When I was a player, but now being a manager, you need to understand that you're going to win and you're going to lose. When you win, you are not the best. And when you lose, you are not the worst. So, this is something that you need to have that balance," said Forlan on the eve of the clash between India and Uruguay."If you talk about us not getting out of the group stage in the last two World Cups, of course, for a national team like Uruguay, with the players we have, it's not good. We understand that. But we know it's football and things happen. Just because we didn't qualify (forward), we are not going to say that they are not good players. You're not going to change the way you are."For Forlan, instilling his philosophy of football is paramount. The Montevideo-born striker played 525 games in his senior career and scored 222 goals. His storied career saw him win Premier League, FA Cup and Community Shield titles with Manchester United; Europa League and UEFA Super Cup with Atletico Madrid and the 2011 Copa America title with Uruguay. As his journey went from Uruguay to England to Spain to Italy to Japan to India to Hong Kong, he picked up plenty of learnings along the way."As a human being you're always learning and getting more experience. As a player I had the opportunity to play in different continents, in great clubs, which I learned a lot, as well as when I was here in India, Hong Kong, and also Japan, and my time in Europe, as well as in South America."So you always try to learn about everybody. I had great teammates, great coaches, and also in my family, my brother, my father. I really enjoyed football when I was playing, really enjoy now watching and being a manager, of course. I want for my team to play well, we have really good players, talented players. And I know that our team has that possibility to play as a good team, to play good football," he explained.At the same time, he stressed that he didn't want to be typecast based on the notions of the way the South American teams of the past played their football. The Uruguayan, who is of Basque, Irish, and Italian descent, pushed for his team to adapt according to the situation, the opposition and where they stand.The 20th ranked team come into the last friendly of this window after a loss (1-3 vs Japan) and win (4-1 vs Korea). With India next, a team much further down the order, Forlan doesn't intend to relax. Equally, he was impressed by India's show against Panama and the first half hour versus Brazil.“India have some really good players. They know what to do,” he said. “There were some really nice combinations. If you give them time and space, they can damage you, and they can play well. So you have to respect everybody. We know it's not going to be easy. Playing here, the weather, the humidity, also you need to adapt."That's why we came early. It was good for us to adapt to this weather, different than Japan and Korea. In a loss to Bishop Fenwick, Zexter carried the ball 25 times for 268 yards and scored 3 touchdowns on runs of 56, 66 and 41 yards. He also connected on 4 PATs.

Previous winners were Appponequet's Beckett Canessa and Bishop Stang's Andrew Guenette.

The winner of the SouthCoast Preseason Offensive Player of the Year poll was Dartmouth's Chase Afonso with 39% of the vote. The winner of the SouthCoast Preseason Defensive Player of the Year poll was Old Rochester's Owen Pelland with 60% of the vote.

Here's your chance to vote for the top high school performance among SouthCoast football players from last week (Oct. 2-3).

Here's a look at last week's top performers (listed in alphabetical order by school):

(Editor's Note: Voting will end on Sunday, Oct. 11 at 8 p.m.)

In a win over Dartmouth, Canessa threw his fifth touchdown pass of the season to keep the Lakers undefeated. He also had a 2-point conversion pass.

For the second straight week, Procaccini scored 5 touchdowns in a win over Dartmouth. They came on runs of 39, 43, 6 and 22 points in addition to catching a 53-yard scoring strike. He also had a 2-point conversion run.

Conceicao returned an interception 57 yards for a touchdown in Stang's win over Arlington Catholic.

Zexter carried the ball 18 times for 256 yards and scored 4 touchdowns on runs of 66, 58, 11 and 55 yards to power the Spartans to their first win of the season against Arlington Catholic. He also connected on 5 PATs.

In a loss to Apponequet, Afonso caught a 45-yard touchdown pass and ran for a 45-yard touchdown.

Gendron threw a 45-yard touchdown pass and connected on three 2-point conversion passes in a loss to undefeated Apponequet.

In addition to catching a 2-point conversion pass to put the Blue Devils ahead by 9 points late, he had an interception on defense to stop West Bridgewater's final scoring attempt.

Joseph carried the ball 18 times for 68 yards and scored a rushing touchdown against West Bridgewater.

Ponte connected on a 60-yard touchdown pass and a 2-point conversion to help the Blue Devils best West Bridgewater.

In a loss to Somerset Berkley, Figueroa threw a pair of touchdown passes and a 2-point conversion.

Libby returned a kickoff 75 yards for a touchdown in Voc-Tech's loss to Somerset Berkley.

In a loss to Quincy, Correia had a one-handed interception on defense.

Ramos scored New Bedford's lone touchdown and 2-point conversion in a loss to Quincy.

In the second half of a loss to Bristol-Plymouth, Foye was 4 of 7 passes for 82 yards and rushed for 40 yards.

Baptiste had an interception on the goal line to set up a 99-yard scoring drive for ORR in a loss to Foxboro.

In a loss to Foxboro, Hiles scored a pair of touchdowns on runs of 1 and 7 yards.

Pires scored 3 rushing touchdowns and a 2-point conversion as the Vikings beat Upper Cape to end their 2-game losing streak.

articles.summary: Follow along with all the action this week.
articles.body:
Midweek action is here. MLS games are available on MLS Season Pass on Apple TV, in addition to any other options listed. All kickoff times are in Eastern time. Let's get into it!

Ecuador vs Panama, 2:30a: Panama ( Elo #54 ) has a friendly with #20 Ecuador.

Italy U21 vs Poland U21, 12:15p: Luca Koleosho is with Italy's U21s for their EURO U21 qualifying matches.

Martinique vs El Salvador, 6p on FS2, Fubo, ViX: El Salvador (#130) visits #131 Martinique in Concacaf Nations League A.

Honduras vs Jamaica, 10p on FS2, TUDN, Fubo, ViX: The Reggae Boyz (#75) visit #77 Honduras in Concacaf Nations League A.

USA vs Canada, 8p on TNT, HBO Max, Peacock, Telemundo, UNIVERSO, Fubo: The headliner! USA (#25) welcome #32 Canada into town for this friendly.

Rotherham vs Bradford, 2p: Julian Eyestone and Rotherham host Bradford in EFL Trophy play.

Stevenage vs Leicester, 2p: Former NYCFC left back Christian McFarlane and Leicester (now in League One) have an EFL Trophy game away at Stevenage.

Chicago Fire vs Vancouver Whitecaps, 8:30p: Brian White, Tate Johnson, and the 'Caps visit Johan Gómez, Sergio Oregel, and the Fire in MLS.

Mexico vs Chile, 10:30p on TUDN, Univision: The team that just lost 3-0 to the USA has a friendly with #44-ranked Chile.

Braunschweig vs Holstein Kiel, 12:30p on ESPN Select, Fubo: John Tolkin and Holstein Kiel visit Eintracht Braunschweig in the 2. Bundesliga.

PSV vs Heerenveen, 2p on ESPN+, Fubo: Sergiño Dest and PSV host Heerenveen in Eredivisie action. Ricardo Pepi is sidelined with a minor muscle injury from September 20th, when he had to come off against Twente after just 8 minutes.

Dortmund vs Werder Bremen, 2:30p on Peacock, UNIVERSO, Fubo, Fandango, Telemundo Deportes: A first chance to see if BVB boss Niko Kovač is impressed enough by Mathis Albert's USA performances to bring him into Bundesliga action yet.

Lens vs Lyon, 2:45p on beIN Sports Español, Fubo: Tanner Tessmann, a young player who wasn't in USA camp this time, travels with Olympique Lyon to visit Lens in Ligue 1.

That's it! Did I miss anything that matters? Let me know in the comments below. Let's see who stands out this week!

articles.standfirst: El ex del Madrid dice no a ofertas de España y de Europa
articles.summary: El ex del Madrid dice no a ofertas de España y de Europa
articles.body: El exdelantero del Real Madrid era agente libre y, en las últimas horas, ha cerrado un acuerdo con el club qatarí. Solo queda a la espera de que se haga oficial. Joselu ha recibido ofertas de varios clubes españoles e italianos en los últimos meses, así como del Eintracht y del Union de Berlín, sin llegar nunca a un acuerdo. Continuará su carrera en Catar tras su exitoso paso por el Al-Gharafa donde pudo anotar 21 goles y fue uno de los delanteros más destacados de toda la liga.
